data.title: Jindal Panther Crowned Indian Masters Champions with Thrilling 12-11 Victory
data.description:
India, Nov. 7 -- Jindal Steel Limited

New Delhi [India], November 7: Jindal Panther were crowned champions of the Indian Masters (14-goal tournament) after a thrilling 12-11 win over Vimal Arion Achievers in a closely contested final that went to extra time.

In a final that had everything, Jindal Panther held a 10-7 advantage heading into the sixth chukker, with Mr Naveen Jindal contributing with two goals, appearing firmly in control of the contest. However, Vimal Arion Achievers mounted a spirited comeback to take an 11-10 lead, putting the championship within their grasp. Demonstrating tremendous composure and fighting spirit, Jindal Panther fought back to level the scores at 11-11, taking the match into extra time.

With the championship at stake, Matt Perry emerged as the match-winner, scoring the decisive golden goal in extra time to secure a memorable 12-11 victory for Jindal Panther and seal the Indian Masters title.

The final was a testament to the competitive spirit and skill of both teams, with Vimal Arion Achievers putting up a spirited challenge and pushing Jindal Panther all the way to the finish.

The victory marks a spectacular end to the season for Jindal Panther, who demonstrated resilience, teamwork and determination to emerge champions of the prestigious 14-goal tournament.

data.title: Elon Musk's bankruptcy warnings collide with JPMorgan's first Bitcoin forecast
data.description:
Elon Musk has a new item on his worry list. The Tesla and SpaceX chief, described by Forbes as the world's first trillionaire, has paired his long-running warnings about financial collapse with fresh fears about an artificial intelligence-driven nightmare.

His latest message is a warning of "global bankruptcy." Forbes suggests it could become a game-changer for the Bitcoin price, and it lands just as JPMorgan rolls out a Bitcoin forecast that Forbes called "extraordinary."

During a February 2026 appearance on the Dwarkesh Podcast, he put his confidence level well past the usual scale.

"We are 1000% going to go bankrupt as a country and fail as a country without AI and robots."

Musk's view is that the US cannot outgrow its debt with today's economy. Only a big jump in productivity from AI and robotics would let the country cover what it owes. Without that jump, he argues, the bill eventually wins.

US national debt passed $40 trillion in late 2026, according to the research findings. Interest payments on that debt are reported to exceed military spending.

This is where Musk's two fears meet. He frames AI as both a possible threat and the only realistic escape hatch from the debt spiral.

JPMorgan Asset Management included Bitcoin in its Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report for the first time in October 2026. That annual report is where the firm lays out its expected returns for major asset classes over the coming decade.

The headline figure: a projected 10% annualized return for Bitcoin through 2036. The research findings note that this outpaces JPMorgan's forecasts for traditional holdings such as large-cap US stocks and bonds.

The reasoning rests on supply. Bitcoin's issuance is capped, while the broader money supply keeps expanding.

That logic lines up neatly with how Musk talks about Bitcoin. He has described it as "based on energy" and contrasted it with fiat currency, which governments can print without a hard limit.

Tesla holds 11,509 BTC, while SpaceX holds 18,712 BTC, according to the research findings. Together that comes to approximately 30,221 BTC, reportedly acquired at low average costs.

That gives Musk a direct stake in how markets interpret his warnings. Few public figures warning about fiscal collapse also run two companies sitting on a large position in the asset most often pitched as a hedge against it.

To be fair, there is no evidence that his statements are designed to move the market. But anyone reading his posts should know where the corporate treasuries sit.

The connection between government debt and Bitcoin is not new. Bitcoin's original design was a response to concerns about centralized money and unchecked issuance.

The research findings are explicit that no single Musk statement has been conclusively tied to an immediate Bitcoin price move.

The most significant development here is arguably JPMorgan's, not Musk's. A formal return assumption from JPMorgan Asset Management is different. Long-term capital market assumptions feed into how advisers and institutions think about portfolio construction. Bitcoin showing up in that framework signals that it is being treated as an asset class worth modeling, rather than a curiosity.

A 10% forecast is also not a guarantee. Forecasts of this kind are long-range estimates, and a decade is plenty of time for assumptions to break.

For now, the practical watch list is short. Track US fiscal policy and debt-servicing costs, monitor whether other large asset managers follow JPMorgan in publishing Bitcoin assumptions, and keep an eye on any changes to Tesla's and SpaceX's holdings.

data.title: FDA Investigates Cancer Risk Associated With Novartis' Zolgensma Gene Therapy
data.description:
BASEL (dpa-AFX) - In medicine, one truth transcends time: a drug's worth is measured not merely by how effectively it fights disease, but also by how safely it does so.

One medicine that has recently drawn the FDA's attention over emerging safety concerns is Novartis Inc.'s (NVS) Zolgensma gene therapy.

Approved in the U.S. in May 2019, Zolgensma is an adeno-associated virus vector-based gene therapy indicated for the treatment of pediatric patients less than 2 years of age with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). Administered as a one-time intravenous infusion, Zolgensma carries a boxed warning for serious liver injury and acute liver failure, including reported fatal cases. Its prescribing information also highlights several other important safety concerns, including elevated aminotransferases, thrombocytopenia, thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), and the potential risk of tumorigenicity associated with AAV vector integration.

More than 6,000 patients have been treated with Zolgensma across clinical trials, managed access programs and commercial treatment, according to Novartis. Priced at $2.125 million for a one-time treatment, Zolgensma made headlines in 2019 as the world's most expensive drug at the time.

On November 5, 2026, Novartis disclosed that it had received nine reports of tumors in patients previously treated with Zolgensma since the therapy's first approval in 2019. Of these, two cases have so far shown evidence of vector DNA integration into the patients' DNA. Both patients have undergone treatment and remain under medical monitoring.

Postmarketing reports of tumor formation (neoplasia) include tumors of the central and peripheral nervous systems, spinal/paraspinal regions, and the kidney. Further investigation revealed that, in two cases, product-related vector DNA integration involved the GLI1 (Glioma-Associated Oncogene Homolog 1) gene, an oncogene that has the potential to cause cancer when overexpressed or abnormally activated. The mechanism underlying GLI1 overexpression in the third case remains under investigation.

Novartis has another approved gene therapy, Itvisma, which uses the same vector and construct as Zolgensma.

Itvisma is indicated for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in adult and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older with a confirmed mutation in the survival motor neuron 1 (SMN1) gene. Administered via intrathecal injection, Itvisma is also an AAV vector-based gene therapy. It was approved by the FDA in November 2025 and is priced at $2.59 million per treatment.

Itvisma carries a boxed warning for acute serious liver injury and elevated aminotransferases. Its prescribing information also includes warnings and precautions regarding hepatotoxicity (liver injury), thrombocytopenia (low platelet count), peripheral sensory neuropathy, thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), elevated cardiac troponin I, and AAV vector integration and the potential risk of tumorigenicity.

During the first nine months of 2026, Novartis reported combined sales of $1.071 billion for its Zolgensma Group, comprising Zolgensma and Itvisma, compared with $925 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

With postmarketing adverse event reports of malignancies in patients treated with Zolgensma, the FDA has begun an investigation of the identified risk of neoplasia, including malignancy, with serious outcomes.

The FDA has determined that the risk of neoplasia, including malignancy, applies to both Zolgensma and Itvisma, as they contain the same vector and construct. To date, no cases of neoplasia have been reported following Itvisma administration.

The overall benefits of both Zolgensma and Itvisma continue to outweigh their potential risks for their respective approved indications. Nevertheless, the agency is evaluating whether further regulatory action is warranted.

As part of this assessment, the FDA is expeditiously reviewing whether Zolgensma's current prescribing information and long-term follow-up studies are adequate to address the newly identified risk of insertional oncogenesis. The agency has also advised that patients treated with the therapy and clinical trial participants be monitored for tumor formation.

According to a review published in the Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics in July of 2026, a total of 78 marketed drugs were withdrawn by the FDA between 1955 and 2026, frequently associated with serious adverse effects.

As the FDA investigation unfolds, the implications for Zolgensma, Itvisma, and the broader landscape of AAV-based gene therapies remain an important area to watch.

NVS closed Friday's (Nov.6, 2026) trading at $162.55, up 0.38%.

data.title: China extends gold buying spree to two years as prices drop, adds 25.8 tonnes in October
data.description:
China’s central bank added to its gold reserves in October — extending a buying streak to two years — as the precious metal fell almost 7% to end the month below the $4,000-an-ounce support threshold.

Bullion holdings at the People’s Bank of China rose by 830,000 ounces in October, or around 25.8 metric tons, according to official data released Saturday. That’s the 24th consecutive month of accumulation. In particular, the central bank has stepped up purchases in recent months as gold prices have slumped, with additions in the first 10 months of the year totaling around 129 metric tons.

PBOC was the biggest disclosed buyer among global central banks in the third quarter, World Gold Council data showed. Cumulative official-sector purchases reported by the WGC were a net 321 tons in the July to September period, the most since the final quarter of 2024. These accumulations remain a key support to gold prices in an otherwise tepid market.

Bullion touched a one-year low last month and recorded its biggest October decline since the global financial crisis in 2008. It’s rebounded since the US midterm elections this week, but remains down by more than a fifth since the Iran war began in late February. Higher energy prices have fueled inflation and led to tighter monetary policy, which is typically a headwind for non-yielding bullion.

PBOC’s holdings influence the buying patterns of Chinese households. Many purchased gold at around $4,000 an ounce in October, expecting that central-bank purchasing would help support prices in the long run.

data.title: Diwali 2026: Stock market enters Samvat 2083 with Nifty 50 above 25,000: Key support, resistance levels. Targets to know
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Indian equity markets are entering Samvat 2083 on a strong footing after an extraordinary week on Dalal Street, with the Nifty 50 reclaiming the psychologically important 25,000 mark and the Sensex crossing 81,000.

Both benchmark indices recorded their biggest weekly gains since February 2021, rising 8.6% and 8.8%, respectively, as a sharp correction in crude oil prices, aggressive foreign fund buying and better-than-expected corporate earnings triggered a broad-based improvement in investor sentiment.

The rally was particularly significant as Indian equities managed to outperform global markets despite a sharp selloff in technology stocks and AI-linked shares. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs), who had remained net sellers for much of 2026, returned aggressively to domestic equities. They purchased shares worth Rs.13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data, taking their purchases over the last five trading sessions to Rs.35,781 crore, according to market estimates.

On Friday, 6 November, the Nifty 50 advanced 493.75 points, or 2.01%, to close at 25,030.35, while the BSE Sensex surged 1,718.01 points, or 2.17%, to settle at 81,028.02. Both indices ended at their highest levels in more than eight months. The Nifty and Sensex also extended their winning streaks to seven consecutive sessions, their longest such runs in 14 months and 26 months, respectively.

Despite the sharp recovery, both benchmarks remain in negative territory for 2026, with the Nifty down 4.2% and the Sensex lower by 4.9%, compared with a 7% gain in the MSCI Emerging Markets index.

With the festive season ushering in Samvat 2083, investors will be watching whether the momentum can be sustained or the sharp rally gives way to some consolidation. What are the key support and resistance levels for the Nifty 50, and how high can the index climb? Here's what market experts and technical analysts expect.

Dr V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments Limited, said the sharp selloff in US technology stocks could have a relatively limited impact on Indian equities, while the slowdown in the global AI trade could work in India's favour.

He attributed the Nasdaq's 5.6% plunge to concerns over a potential slowdown in data centre spending amid political opposition to large-scale investments in the sector in the US. According to him, the resulting correction in technology and AI-linked stocks could benefit markets such as India, which have relatively limited exposure to the global AI trade.

Vijayakumar noted that FIIs had purchased Indian equities worth Rs.35,781 crore over the preceding five trading sessions. He expects domestic markets to remain resilient if foreign buying continues, even as domestic institutional investors (DIIs) book profits.

He also highlighted that the ongoing rally is fundamentally supported by better-than-expected corporate earnings growth.

"An important factor investors should recognise is that this rally is being driven by large-cap stocks, which had become attractively valued," Vijayakumar said.

He pointed to the divergence between large- and small-cap stocks, noting that while the Sensex rallied 2.6% in the previous session, the Nifty Smallcap 100 index gained only 0.67%. This indicates that institutional money is increasingly moving towards large-cap stocks.

Vijayakumar sees further upside potential in financial, technology and automobile stocks.

Osho Krishan, Chief Manager - Technical and Derivatives Research at Angel One, said the Nifty 50 has staged a sharp vertical rally, decisively moving above all its key exponential moving averages (EMAs) and the 200-day simple moving average (200-DSMA).

However, momentum indicators have entered overbought territory, suggesting that investors should exercise caution at current levels. Krishan said some profit booking cannot be ruled out, but any such correction should be viewed as a healthy consolidation that could help sustain the broader bullish trend.

On the downside, he identified the 24,770-24,500 zone as immediate support, while the bullish gap around 24,300 remains a crucial support level.

On the upside, 25,150 could act as an intermediate hurdle, followed by resistance near 25,400.

Looking ahead, Krishan advised traders to adopt a stock-specific approach, particularly during the festive season and the truncated trading week. With the market having rallied sharply and technical indicators showing overbought conditions, he recommended a conservative approach and disciplined risk management.

"With most of the easy gains already captured, selective participation and prudent position sizing will be key," he said.

Rajesh Bhosale, Technical Analyst at My Advisor Alpha, said the sharp market recovery was driven by a combination of favourable global developments, aggressive foreign institutional buying and the unwinding of accumulated short positions.

He attributed the rally to the Democrats' sweeping victory in the US midterm elections, securing control of both the House and the Senate, which raised hopes of an early resolution to the US-Iran conflict. This triggered a sharp decline in crude oil prices from their six-month highs, providing significant relief to an oil-importing economy such as India.

Bhosale also highlighted the return of foreign investors, who had been persistent sellers through October, noting that they purchased around Rs.15,000 crore worth of Indian equities on Thursday alone. The unwinding of short positions further amplified the rally.

He said market sentiment had undergone a sharp turnaround in just a few weeks. The Nifty 50, which was struggling near its multi-year swing low of 22,200-22,500, has now reclaimed 25,000 and moved decisively above its major moving averages.

The index has also confirmed a bullish double-bottom breakout, while its daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) has surged above 78 from below 40 in just a week, indicating strong upward momentum.

"Given the pattern breakout, the positive momentum is likely to continue. However, after such a sharp rally and with overbought conditions in place, traders should adopt a buy-on-dips approach," Bhosale said.

He identified 24,800 as immediate support, which also marks the breakout zone. On the upside, 25,400-25,500 is the key resistance band. A decisive move above this zone could open the way towards 26,000 and fresh all-time highs.

Bhosale added that the latest rally was largely driven by heavyweight stocks, while participation from the mid-cap segment remained relatively limited. Going ahead, he expects the Nifty to consolidate after its sharp gains, with individual stocks, particularly mid-caps, potentially leading the next leg of the rally.

data.title: AstraZeneca Pharma India Reports 30% Revenue Growth, Crosses Rs 7,291 Mn
data.description:
Strong performance across oncology, biopharmaceuticals and rare diseases, alongside regulatory approvals and state-level healthcare partnerships, drives growth

AstraZeneca Pharma India Limited reported a 30 per cent year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 7,291 million in the second quarter of FY2026-27, covering July to September 2026, driven by sustained performance across its oncology, biopharmaceuticals and rare disease portfolios. The company also reported a 30 per cent increase in revenue for the first half of FY2026-27, reaching Rs 14,119 million, compared with Rs 10,854 million in the corresponding period last year. The company attributed its performance to operational efficiency, portfolio expansion and increasing adoption of innovative therapies addressing unmet medical needs in India.

Oncology remained the largest contributor, generating Rs 5,085 million in Q2, compared with Rs 3,978 million in the year-ago quarter. Revenue from biopharmaceuticals, covering cardiovascular, renal and metabolism (CVRM), respiratory and immunology (R&I), and vaccines and immunotherapies (V&I), stood at Rs 1,610 million, against Rs 1,268 million previously. The rare diseases segment recorded revenue of Rs 204 million, compared with Rs 38 million in the corresponding quarter last year.

Regulatory Approvals And Expansion

Commenting on the results, Praveen Rao Akkinepally, Country President and Managing Director, AstraZeneca Pharma India, said the growth reflected the strength of the company's science-led portfolio and its ability to translate innovation into meaningful patient outcomes.

During the quarter, the company secured multiple regulatory approvals, including new indications for trastuzumab deruxtecan across HER2-positive breast cancer settings. Approvals were also received for benralizumab for hypereosinophilic syndrome and acalabrutinib-based combinations for previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and mantle cell lymphoma.

The company also expanded its healthcare partnerships through memoranda of understanding with the governments of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. These collaborations aim to strengthen oncology care, genomic testing and AI-enabled lung cancer screening across public healthcare facilities.

Other initiatives included K+ Connect, focused on hyperkalaemia management among patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease, and India Coronary Conquest 2026, aimed at strengthening cardiovascular care through clinician-led learning. AstraZeneca Pharma India also received recognition at the OPPI India Awards 2026 for its rare disease contributions and at the ETHRWorld Employee Experience Awards 2026, where it secured a Gold Award.

data.title: Culture Evolves When People Act Without Reminders: Alembic CHRO On Lasting Change
data.description:
Namita Patwari says lasting change needs employee involvement, visible leadership commitment and open feedback, and that the real test of a cultural shift is what people do when no one is reminding them of the new behaviours

At 115 years old, Alembic Pharmaceuticals is evolving without letting go of what defines it. Namita Patwari, CHRO and Chief Customer Experience Officer, says HR’s job is to protect trust, integrity, commitment and purpose while building the digital fluency, analytical thinking and adaptability pharma will need. She explains how AI-enabled learning through RepReadyAI is strengthening field execution, why wellbeing must be built into how work is organised and not run as a stand-alone programme, and why a culture has truly shifted only when people act on new behaviours without being reminded. She also outlines what HR should do early to make mergers and partnerships work, beginning with listening.

A 115-year-old company keeps evolving without losing its identity. Which elements of a long-standing culture should HR deliberately protect as the business changes?

The strength of a legacy organisation lies in evolving while staying true to its values. At Alembic, over a century of growth has been guided by trust, integrity, commitment, and purpose. HR plays a key role in preserving this legacy while adapting to changing employee expectations and business needs. Culture is reflected in everyday actions, leadership decisions, and how employees feel respected, valued, and included. A strong legacy fosters belonging and pride while creating opportunities for growth, enabling employees to contribute meaningfully to the organisation’s future.

Which capabilities will pharma need most over the next five years, and how should HR build them across R&D, manufacturing, and commercial teams?

I believe the pharmaceutical industry will increasingly require digital fluency, analytical thinking, technical expertise, and adaptability. Equally important is the ability to learn continuously and apply knowledge effectively in everyday work. At Alembic, our RepReadyAI initiative reflects how technology can make learning more interactive, practical, and engaging.

For me, the real value of learning lies not in completing a programme, but in how confidently employees apply their knowledge, improve their performance, and grow in their roles. Learning outcomes should be measurable through stronger on-the-job application, improved productivity, enhanced quality of execution, and increased readiness for larger responsibilities.

HR must create opportunities for continuous learning through relevant development programmes, practical exposure, and regular feedback. We must also help employees prepare for evolving responsibilities and future career opportunities. Equally important is tracking the effectiveness of learning through indicators such as skill proficiency, performance improvements, internal mobility, succession readiness, and the successful application of new capabilities in the workplace. When people are equipped to grow alongside the business and learning outcomes are translated into tangible results, capability building becomes an investment in both individual development and organisational resilience.

As AI takes over more routine HR work, how will the role of the CHRO change in the next few years?

I see AI as an opportunity to make HR more proactive, efficient, and data-driven by simplifying routine processes and enabling greater focus on leadership development, workforce planning, capability building, and employee experience. In pharma, AI can help identify skill gaps across functions, anticipate future capability needs, personalise learning, and strengthen talent pipelines. At Alembic, RepReadyAI demonstrates how AI-enabled, practice-based learning can strengthen scientific knowledge, customer engagement, and field execution among sales representatives.

However, the human dimension of HR will remain critical. While AI can provide insights, understanding employee aspirations, building trust, coaching leaders, and making sensitive people decisions require empathy and judgement. CHROs must ensure technology complements human capabilities while helping employees develop digital fluency and adaptability.

Ultimately, AI’s value must be measured through tangible outcomes, including faster onboarding and hiring, improved learning effectiveness and field productivity, stronger GMP and compliance training adherence, better succession readiness, and enhanced employee engagement. Used thoughtfully, AI can enable better decisions and build a more agile, responsive, and future-ready organisation.

How can wellbeing become part of the way work is organised, rather than a stand-alone programme?

I believe wellbeing is shaped by everyday work experiences-how we respect people’s time, understand their needs, and support them through different stages of life. At Alembic, the eight-hour workday and period-related work-from-home flexibility reflect this focus. I believe such measures recognise employees’ diverse needs and responsibilities while enabling them to contribute effectively.

For me, a supportive culture also means creating an environment where employees can raise concerns comfortably and managers lead with empathy. For example, a manager adjusting a deadline when an employee faces a personal challenge demonstrates how small, thoughtful actions can make wellbeing part of everyday work. Policies provide the framework, but their impact lies in how they are practised. I believe wellbeing must be reflected in daily decisions, team interactions, and opportunities for growth and not treated as a stand-alone HR initiative.

With your grounding in organisation development, what makes a change initiative last, and what tells you a culture has genuinely shifted?

One of the most important lessons I have learnt is that change cannot be sustained through communication alone. People embrace change when they understand its purpose, see its relevance to their work, and witness leaders consistently demonstrating the expected behaviours. In my experience, lasting change requires employee involvement, visible leadership commitment, and opportunities to share feedback and concerns. When employees feel heard and included, they take ownership rather than view change as something imposed on them.

For me, a real cultural shift is reflected in everyday actions like how teams collaborate, take accountability, make decisions, and express different viewpoints. While engagement scores and employee feedback are useful indicators, I believe the true measure of success lies in what people do when no one is reminding them what the new behaviours should be. Change becomes sustainable when these behaviours become part of the organisation's way of working and are reflected naturally in how people think, interact and contribute every day. That, to me, is when culture has genuinely evolved.

As companies grow through partnerships and acquisitions, what should HR put in place early so that different cultures come together well?

I believe successful cultural integration begins with listening. Every organisation has its own strengths, values and working styles, and HR should understand these before deciding how to bring people together. A culture and working-style assessment of both organisations, done early, gives integration decisions a factual base. Early on, HR must give clarity on roles, reporting lines, communication channels and growth opportunities, and commit to timelines for each. Uncertainty is where people disengage or leave, so concerns should be addressed openly, with critical talent engaged first and regular forums such as town halls and Q&As where employees can ask questions and get honest answers.

I would place strong emphasis on leadership alignment. Leaders from both sides should present a consistent message and model the behaviours expected. A joint integration team, along with cross-team projects built around shared goals, helps relationships form through real work. Integration should not mean overlooking the strengths each group brings; the aim is to keep what works from both and build a common purpose people can connect with. Ultimately, integration succeeds when employees see a place for themselves in the organisation’s future and understand how they can contribute to it. That sense of belonging is what holds a combined organisation together.

Savi Khanna

data.title: Amber Enterprises Arm IL JIN Electronics Files DRHP For Rs 2,500 Cr IPO
data.description:
Amber Enterprises subsidiary plans a Rs 2,500 crore fresh issue to pare debt, fund manufacturing equipment purchases and support capacity expansion across its electronics manufacturing operations.

IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd, a subsidiary of Amber Enterprises India Ltd, has filed draft papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to raise Rs 2,500 crore through an initial public offering (IPO), according to its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6.

The proposed IPO will comprise entirely a fresh issue of equity shares, with no offer for sale (OFS) component, meaning the proceeds will go to the company.

IL JIN Electronics plans to use the IPO proceeds to repay or prepay outstanding borrowings, along with accrued interest, availed by the company and its subsidiaries, Ascent Circuits and Shogini Technoarts. The funds will also be deployed towards purchasing plant, machinery and equipment for its manufacturing facilities, besides meeting general corporate requirements.

The company operates as a vertically integrated electronics design and manufacturing services provider across four business segments: electronics manufacturing services (EMS), bare printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing, power electronics and industrial automation.

IL JIN Electronics currently operates 11 manufacturing facilities, including 10 in India and one in Israel. Its domestic manufacturing footprint spans Noida and Greater Noida in Uttar Pradesh, Pune in Maharashtra, Chennai and Hosur in Tamil Nadu, and Bengaluru in Karnataka.

The company also has six manufacturing facilities under construction, which are expected to add to its production capacity as it expands operations.

Financially, IL JIN Electronics reported revenue from operations of Rs 3,268.47 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 1,240.41 crore in FY24.

Its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased to Rs 321.07 crore in FY26 from Rs 71.42 crore in FY24, reflecting an expansion in both its business scale and operating earnings over the two-year period.

Amber Enterprises is a major player in India's room air-conditioner original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and original design manufacturer (ODM) market. The proposed listing of IL JIN Electronics will provide the group with a separate listed platform for its electronics manufacturing operations.

Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, Axis Capital and Jefferies India have been appointed as the book-running lead managers for the IPO, while KFin Technologies will serve as the registrar to the issue.

data.title: Lemon Tree Hotels reports highest-ever Q2 revenue and profitability
data.description:
Lemon Tree Hotels Limited has announced its unaudited results for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026, reporting its highest-ever Q2 room rates, revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT and cash profit. Growth was driven by its owned hotels and managed and franchised portfolio.

For Q2 FY27, total revenue grew 18 per cent to Rs 363.8 crore, and net EBITDA increased 22 per cent to Rs 162.2 crore, with net EBITDA margin rising 157 bps to 44.6 per cent. Before the impact of GST changes and the provision for stock appreciation rights, which together came to 3.2 per cent of revenue, net EBITDA grew 31 per cent to Rs 173.7 crore, with a margin of 47.7 per cent.

PBT before exceptional items grew 59 per cent to Rs 88.8 crore, PAT increased 90 per cent to Rs 79.8 crore, and cash profit rose 28 per cent to Rs 97.2 crore. RevPAR grew 18 per cent to Rs 5,137, supported by an 8 per cent increase in average room rate to Rs 6,751 and a 633-bps gain in occupancy to 76.1 per cent. Owned hotels recorded 15 per cent revenue growth to Rs 337 crore, while hotel EBITDAR margin increased 112 bps to 53 per cent.

Commenting on the results, Neelendra Singh, Managing Director, Lemon Tree Hotels, said, “Q2 has been a strong quarter for Lemon Tree Hotels, with our highest-ever Q2 revenue, EBITDA and profitability. Revenue grew by 18 per cent and Net EBITDA grew 22 per cent, with margins expanding by 157 basis points while absorbing the impact of GST changes and stock appreciation rights. Room rates grew by 8 per cent and occupancy climbed by more than six percentage points to 76.1 per cent.

The simultaneous growth in room rates and occupancy reflects the strength of our brands and the effectiveness of our distribution network and loyalty programme in bringing guests back. Together, these are the engines driving performance across our portfolio and also creating value for our owner partners. We signed 825 rooms and opened 523 rooms in Q2; while fees from third-party hotels grew 30 per cent. As the New India Traveller seeks increasingly differentiated hospitality experiences, our pipeline is expanding in step with this demand, such as Aurika in Shimla, Shillong and Varanasi to Lemon Tree Premier in Bandra, Mumbai.”

For H1 FY27, total revenue grew 14 per cent to Rs 710.6 crore, net EBITDA increased 14 per cent to Rs 314.0 crore, PAT rose 52 per cent to Rs 137.1 crore, and cash profit grew 22 per cent to Rs 193.2 crore. Management fees increased 20 per cent to Rs 86.1 crore, comprising Rs 41.5 crore from third-party-owned hotels, up 36 per cent, and Rs 44.7 crore from Fleur Hotels, up 8 per cent.

RevPAR grew across every brand in the owned portfolio: Aurika recorded 17 per cent growth, Lemon Tree Premier 18 per cent, Lemon Tree Hotels 15 per cent, Red Fox 21 per cent and Keys 29 per cent. Aurika and Lemon Tree Premier together contributed 63 per cent of owned-hotel EBITDAR on 58 per cent of revenue, with Aurika recording a hotel EBITDAR margin of 59 per cent. The Keys portfolio delivered a hotel EBITDAR margin of 50 per cent. Fees from third-party-owned hotels grew 30 per cent to Rs 18.7 crore, while total network revenue across owned, managed and franchised hotels increased 23 per cent to Rs 573 crore.

During Q2, the company opened eight managed and franchised hotels with 523 rooms and signed 11 hotels with 825 rooms, about 1.6 times the inventory opened during the quarter. As of September 30, 2026, its combined operational and pipeline portfolio stood at 285 hotels and 24,061 rooms across 170+ cities. Of these, 138 hotels with 12,131 rooms across 80+ cities were operational.

The company acquired land in Bandra (East), Mumbai, next to BKC, for about Rs 120 crore to develop Lemon Tree Premier, Bandra, an owned 172-room upscale hotel. It will be the group’s seventh hotel in Mumbai and its first in Bandra, with opening expected in FY30. Aurika, Shimla, an owned 90-room hotel, is expected to open in FY27, followed by Aurika, Shillong (165 rooms) in FY28 and Aurika, Varanasi (47 rooms, heritage) in FY29.

Gross debt as of September 30, 2026, stood at Rs 1,429.2 crore, down 11 per cent from Rs 1,610.2 crore a year earlier. Cost of debt fell 28 bps to 7.44 per cent, while debt to equity improved to 0.64x from 0.86x.

On the ESG front, 100 per cent of the company’s 41 owned and leased hotels are green building certified, up from 34 per cent in FY25. Renewable energy accounted for 39.4 per cent of energy use in FY26, compared with 17.0 per cent in FY25, against a target of 50 per cent.

data.title: Tata Steel net up 18% in Q2 on better realisation
data.description:
Tata Steel has reported that its net profit (attributed to owners) in the September quarter was up 18 per cent at ₹3,660 crore against ₹3,102 crore logged in the same period last year, on the back of better realisation.

Revenue increased 12 per cent to₹64,974 crore (₹58,216 crore). EBITDA was up at ₹10,665 crore (₹9,106 crore). EBITDA per tonne jumped to ₹13,462 (₹11,518 crore).

Noel Naval Tata will retire as the Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director and Vice Chairman of the company’s board, on November 11. He has been associated with the company since March 2022, said the company.

Capex projects

The company spent about ₹3,280 crore on capital expenditure during the quarter and ₹6,860 crore in the first half of this fiscal. Significant capex projects underway include 4.8 MTPA capacity expansion at Neelachal Ispat Nigam and downstream growth projects such as the 0.7 MTPA Hot Rolled Pickling and Galvanising Line and 300 kt of the Tinplate expansion, said the company.

Gross debt of the company increased to ₹1.02 lakh crore against ₹97,985 crore in the June quarter. The company had cash and cash equivalents of ₹10,301 crore and a mark-to-market gain of ₹644 crore in currency hedge, leading to a net debt of ₹91,423 crore.

Net debt stood at ₹91,423 crore. Our group liquidity remains strong at ₹40,076 crore, which includes cash and cash equivalents of ₹10,300 crore.

Strong growth

TV Narendran, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, said despite ongoing geoeconomic uncertainty and higher raw material costs, the company delivered strong growth in deliveries and earnings this quarter, backed by a resilient supply chain and close customer engagement.

In the Netherlands, the successful restart of the Direct Sheet Plant and its return to rated capacity have supported improvements in both the product mix and cost profile, he said.

“In the UK, while the Llanwern pickle line is now fully operational, the market conditions continue to be influenced by elevated imports and inventory build-up across parts of the value chain. We remain engaged with policymakers and regulators to support a more balanced and sustainable market environment,” he added.

Koushik Chatterjee, Executive Director & Chief Financial Officer, said Neelachal Ispat Nigam generated EBITDA of ₹318 crore, and the amalgamation of NINL with Tata Steel remains on track for completion during the financial year, subject to final NCLT approval.

In the Netherlands, EBITDA improved from €4 million in Q1 to €72 million in Q2, aided by favourable pricing and the restart of the Direct Sheet Plant in early August, he said.

In the UK, subdued demand and elevated inventories across the supply chain weighed on volumes and performance, he added.

data.title: Quess Corp Reports 15% Revenue Growth In General Staffing Business
data.description:
The staffing company's consolidated revenue rose 15 per cent to Rs 4,396 crore, while profit after tax increased 44 per cent

Quess Corp crossed the 5-lakh workforce milestone in the second quarter of FY27, with its total headcount reaching approximately 5.04 lakh at the end of September 2026. The company added more than 20,000 associates to its general staffing business during the quarter, alongside securing 116 new client contracts.

The company's total headcount increased from 4.83 lakh in the year-ago quarter, marking a year-on-year rise of around 4 per cent, according to its Q2 FY27 earnings release.

General Staffing Drives Growth

The general staffing business reported a headcount of approximately 4.90 lakh during the quarter. It generated revenue of Rs 3,823 crore, up 15 per cent year-on-year, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 23 per cent to Rs 57 crore.

The segment's workforce comprises associates recruited, employed or managed by Quess and deployed at client organisations to meet their staffing requirements. These employees work across sectors including manufacturing, retail, telecom, banking, financial services and insurance.

Consolidated Performance Improves

Quess announced its second-quarter financial results on 30 October 2026, reporting consolidated revenue of Rs 4,396 crore, a 15 per cent year-on-year increase.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 20 per cent to Rs 92 crore, while profit after tax increased 44 per cent to Rs 75 crore.

GCCs Drive Professional Staffing

In the professional staffing segment, global capability centres (GCCs) contributed 71 per cent of both headcount and revenue. Banking, financial services and insurance, along with technology-related verticals, emerged as key growth areas.

The segment added 27 new client contracts during the quarter.

data.title: Samvat to Samvat: Nifty ends lower, while pharma and metals shine
data.description:
The Indian stock market ended the Samvat on a weak note, but a strong rally in the final seven days helped reduce what could have been a much steeper decline. The Nifty closed the Samvat about 4% lower, while the Sensex fell around 5%.

Without the sharp recovery in the last week, the picture would have been far worse for investors. The rally provided some relief after a difficult year for the broader market.

However, not all parts of the market performed poorly. Midcap and smallcap indices managed to deliver positive returns for the Samvat. The Nifty Bank also turned positive, helped by the strong gains in the final few days.

Among sectors, pharma was the clear winner, with the Nifty Pharma index rising 24% during the Samvat. Metal stocks also had a strong year, with the sector gaining 23%. PSU banks and media were among the other better-performing sectors.

On the other hand, FMCG stocks had a difficult year, with the sector falling 18%. The Nifty IT index ended the Samvat 7% lower, although a recent recovery helped limit the losses. Realty, PSU stocks and financial services also ended the year in the red.

At the stock level, BSE emerged as the top performer on the Nifty, rising 53%. Shriram Finance, Titan, Adani Ports and Tech Mahindra also delivered strong returns of between 25% and 40%, significantly outperforming the benchmark index.

The biggest laggard was ITC, which fell 31% during the Samvat. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, HDFC Life and Max Healthcare were among the other major losers. Insurance stocks, in particular, faced pressure, with some names ending the year with losses of more than 20%.

Click here to watch the full video

Overall, the final seven-day rally helped cushion the blow for investors. While the headline indices ended the Samvat lower, several sectors and individual stocks still delivered healthy returns, offering investors pockets of opportunity in an otherwise challenging year.

data.title: E20 petrol meets prescribed quality norms; 893 samples across 27 States and UTs found compliant
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- All 893 samples of E20 petrol drawn from public sector oil marketing companies across 27 States and Union Territories have conformed to prescribed quality standards, refuting claims of excessive ethanol blending, according to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

The clarification follows assertions by the Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology, Government of Karnataka, which claimed that motor spirit sold at specific retail outlets in the state contained between 26 per cent and 31 per cent ethanol.

Three state-run Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited, and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited, highlighted that ethanol blending is a controlled and automated process operating under statutory guidelines rather than manual interventions.

Quality monitoring conducted by the Centre for High Technology under the Ministry established that fuel drawn from 330 IOCL, 280 BPCL, and 283 HPCL retail points complied with the mandated 19 per cent to 21 per cent range under Bureau of Indian Standards specification IS 17021. Within Karnataka, all 56 tested samples registered an average blending level of 19.30 per cent.

The Ministry said that the October 2026 exercise conducted in Karnataka bypassed statutory sampling procedures set out in the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel Control Order, 2005, and the Marketing Discipline Guidelines 2024.

The Ministry noted that the prescribed procedure requires six one-litre samples to be drawn, with two samples handed over to the dealer against acknowledgement, two retained by the oil company or department, and two sent to a laboratory specified under Schedule III of the Control Order or notified in the Official Gazette.

It added that the state authorities failed to share retention samples, outlet details, or certified laboratory documentation.

"The certificates cited in the Karnataka press release merely mention 'Ethanol % by Gas Chromatography', without specifying the applicable standard test method, the prescribed dilution procedure or the reference material used for correction," the Ministry said, pointing out that without these parameters, the figures cannot be validated under IS 17021.

Technical assessments also flagged inconsistencies in density figures reported by the third-party facility, which ranged between 0.742 and 0.749 g/cc, despite higher ethanol content naturally increasing blend density.

Addressing projections regarding vehicle damage and consumer financial impact, official studies conducted with the Automotive Research Association of India and the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers show actual mileage reductions stay within 1 per cent to 6 per cent depending on vehicle calibration. Over 34 crore vehicles operate on the fuel nationwide without widespread mechanical failures.

During the ethanol supply year 2025-26 ending October 31, 2026, state refiners blended 1,134 crore litres of ethanol. The Ministry noted that excess blending provides no commercial rationale, as procuring additional ethanol directly increases procurement expenditure for the oil companies.

OMCs have rejected claims by the Karnataka government that petrol sold at certain retail outlets in the state contains 26-31 per cent ethanol, as per a separate release by the OMCs.

The three OMCs asserted that E20 petrol supplied nationwide complies with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) specification IS 17021, rejecting the Karnataka government's claim that petrol sold at certain retail outlets in the state contains 26-31 per cent ethanol.

"The OMCs would like to clarify that the claims, as reported, are not supported by testing conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures. E20 petrol supplied by the three OMCs across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline," the release said.

data.title: SBI expands US footprint with new branch in Texas
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- State Bank of India expanded its banking subsidiary footprint in the United States with the inauguration of a new branch of SBIC Bank in Frisco, North Dallas, Texas.

The branch, inaugurated by SBI Chairman Challa Sreenivasulu Setty, represents the subsidiary's first office outside California and takes its total branch count in the country from seven to eight.

Beyond the eight subsidiary branches, SBI operates three direct branches in New York, Chicago, and Los Angeles, alongside a representative office in Washington, DC.

The lender selected Dallas because the city serves as a major commercial centre, setting up the outpost to handle retail deposits, commercial lending, remittances across the globe, and specialised services for Non-Resident Indians.

Chairman Challa Sreenivasulu Setty addressed the gathering at the inaugural event, pointing to the institution's strategic shift in the North American market.

"The inauguration of SBIC Bank's Texas branch marks a significant milestone in SBI's international growth journey," Setty said.

He stated that the geographic diversification aligns directly with broader economic objectives between the two countries.

"Our expansion beyond California reflects our commitment to strengthen our presence in strategically important markets, serving the vibrant local communities, Indian diaspora, and supporting the banking needs of individuals and businesses," Setty noted.

He added, "It further reinforces our role in deepening financial and economic ties between India and the United States."

The lender's broader international footprint comprises 245 overseas points of presence spread across 29 countries, encompassing branches, sub-offices, representative units, subsidiaries, and joint ventures.

SBI also maintains correspondent banking arrangements with 222 financial institutions across 56 nations to support cross-border trade settlements and payment transfers.

Digital operations continue through SBI's YONO Global application, which operates across 14 overseas offices and subsidiaries. For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, foreign advances rose 22.86 per cent year-on-year to Rs 8,31,332 crore, while deposit mobilisation at overseas branches registered a 22.61 per cent increase to reach Rs 2,83,319 crore.

data.title: Who is Angan Guha? Ex-Wipro and Chicago Booth biz leader now CEO for Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit - Achievements
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Indian IT major Wipro on Friday announced the appointment of Angan Guha as president and chief executive officer (CEO) of its Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit. Effective 8 December 2026, he will report to Wipro CEO and Managing Director Srini Pallia and will also serve on the company's Executive Leadership Team.

The appointment marks Guha's return to Wipro, where he spent nearly three decades. According to the company's release, he will focus on building business and market momentum across the banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), Energy & Utilities, and Manufacturing sectors. His responsibilities will include accelerating growth, deepening client relationships and delivering greater value to Wipro's clients in the region.

Guha will succeed Suzanne Dann, who was appointed head of the unit in October 2022. Dann left the company in May 2026, Reuters reported.

The appointment comes at a time when revenue growth in Wipro's Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit has slowed, as clients cut back on discretionary spending amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties.

As of the quarter ended 30 September 2026, Americas 2 accounted for 25.6% of Wipro's total revenue, making it the company's third-largest strategic market unit by revenue contribution.

Speaking about his appointment, Guha said, "I am honored and excited to rejoin Wipro at such a pivotal time for our industry." He added, "The evolving AI landscape presents unprecedented opportunities for businesses to innovate and lead. I look forward to collaborating with the talented team at Wipro and helping clients navigate this transformation, drive meaningful business outcomes, and build on Wipro's strong consulting and technology capabilities."

Commenting on the appointment, Pallia said, "We are delighted to welcome Angan to Wipro's leadership team," adding, "His experience in driving business growth, combined with his focus on innovation and execution, will be valuable as we strengthen our Americas business. I am confident that his leadership will help us accelerate growth, deepen client relationships, and deliver greater value to our clients."

Wipro describes Guha as an experienced technology and business leader with more than three decades of experience in driving growth, digital transformation, and client success across the BFSI, Energy & Utilities, and Manufacturing sectors.

According to his LinkedIn profile, Guha studied at G.D. Somani Memorial School before pursuing a Bachelor of Engineering in Electronics Engineering from Savitribai Phule Pune University. He also completed management programmes at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business.

Before joining Wipro, Guha worked as a marketing executive at Decibels Electronics. According to a regulatory filing by Birlasoft, he joined Wipro in 1994 as an account manager and went on to hold several leadership positions during his nearly three-decade tenure.

According to Guha's profile on Wipro's website, he held leadership roles across India, the UK and the US. He went on to lead Wipro's Americas 2 business unit as its CEO and served on the company's Group Executive Council and Executive Board.

In December 2022, Guha joined Birlasoft as its CEO and managing director. He was responsible for providing strategic leadership and driving the company's growth and transformation.

1. FROM MY DESK

President Trump has responded to a stunning midterm defeat by elevating one of his most combative advisers.

Stephen Miller, the architect of Trump's aggressive immigration policies, is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Wiles was seen as a moderating force on the president. Miller, by contrast, has long advocated a no-holds-barred approach to governing.

With Democrats taking control of Congress, Miller is expected to push for greater use of executive power and a confrontational response to congressional investigations. Our reporters explain why his appointment signals that Trump has little intention of changing course after the election.

And for a closer look at the man stepping into one of Washington's most powerful jobs, here are five things to know about Miller.

This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you're not subscribed, sign up here. If you're reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES

  • With Wiles's departure, big business has lost a sympathetic ear in the White House.
  • Vice President JD Vance and Gulf allies are pressing Trump to end the Iran war, but other advisers are making the case for renewed attacks.
  • Elon Musk-run companies like SpaceX and Tesla have flourished in Texas thanks to white-glove treatment from elected officials. But that is about to change, Texas Democrats say.
  • A dirty tricks campaign rattled Europe this week, leaving officials convinced a barrage of bomb threats and cyberattacks are coordinated. The thing they can't figure out: Who's behind it?
  • The co-pilot in the Florida Learjet crash was 20-year-old Nathalia Filgueiras. Her dedication to flying in her teens wasn't an anomaly, but part of a growing wave of young people getting an early start in their pilot careers.
  • Jacked up by protein-heavy diet trends and a multitude of wellness fads, breakfast these days is increasingly likely to resemble its far heftier cousin: dinner.

3. FROM THE MARKETS

  • This week brought AI investors to the brink, as Democrats' midterm victories supercharged anxieties that had been building in the run-up to the vote. Thursday's selloff erased $2.5 trillion in market value from the Nasdaq composite, pushing it into correction territory. Hedge funds dumped positions, while systematic trades amplified the losses.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST

The U.S. is emerging as the last true profit engine for the world's carmakers.

Volkswagen is considering making its first American pickup in 40 years, while Nissan is promising more rugged SUVs. Automakers around the world are focused on the U.S. because of Americans' proclivity for large vehicles and SUVs, as well as their willingness to swallow record-high sticker prices. So what happened? As Sharon Terlep reports, China's auto market faces a massive overcapacity crisis, and low-cost vehicles have conquered overseas markets and battered European automakers. Now, with rivals targeting the U.S., Detroit automakers are racing to maintain their high margins in the heartland.

5.

The midterms have given new life to an enduring American tradition.

For generations, Franklin D. Roosevelt and Ronald Reagan shaped American politics with visions that were different in detail but harmonious in principle. Both understood that a big, complicated, disputatious country requires negotiation, nuance and a willingness to live with less than what you want. This week's Democratic victories are evidence that "the battered heart of American democracy is still beating," writes Pulitzer Prize-winning biographer Jon Meacham. His essay for the Journal examines how the midterms have revived a tradition of democratic competition and what it means for the country's future.

6. SEE THE STORY

Democrats broke the 2028 map wide open.

The wave election that gave Democrats control of Congress and a majority of governors' offices is creating another big benefit for the party: new pathways to the White House in 2028. Democratic victories in Texas, Ohio and Iowa have scrambled early thinking about how to garner the 270 Electoral College votes needed to win. The party also won governor's races in all six familiar presidential swing states. Here's a look at the expanded battleground and the new electoral math.

46 square miles

That is how much territory Russian forces have gained in Ukraine this year through the end of October, compared with 1,874 square miles in 2025, according to the Institute for the Study of War. For the past two months, Russian forces have lost more land than they gained as Ukraine's midrange strikes have pummeled supply routes behind the front lines with a variety of drones. 9. AND FINALLY...

Here's the reading list for the hottest class at Harvard.

After our recent article about the surge in popularity of a humanities course for Harvard freshmen, readers asked us for the syllabus. And we're happy to oblige. The selections range from Homer's "The Odyssey" to James Baldwin's "The Fire Next Time." Consider this your invitation to take on a Harvard reading challenge of your own.

data.title: Fidelity's Jurrien Timmer favors Bitcoin over gold amid sell-off
data.description:
Bitcoin and gold both took a hit in the latest market sell-off. According to Fidelity's Jurrien Timmer, only one of them handled it with any grace.

Timmer, Fidelity's Director of Global Macro, says he prefers Bitcoin over gold right now. His reasoning is simple: Bitcoin's price measured against gold has held up while both assets slid.

Timmer isn't saying Bitcoin went up while gold went down. Both assets declined during the sell-off, which the research places around November 6-7.

His focus is the ratio between them. On that scoreboard, Bitcoin looks strong. One Bitcoin bought approximately 12 ounces of gold at its low point in this cycle. It now buys roughly 21 ounces.

The move has also pushed Bitcoin above the recent trading range it held against gold. For technical analysts, a break like that often signals a change in leadership between two assets.

Timmer has a habit of tracking these shifts closely. He has recorded several rotations of speculative capital between Bitcoin and gold since late 2025.

Those rotations picked up after Bitcoin peaked close to $126,000 in 2025 and gold's own momentum began to fade.

Timmer's preference lines up with where institutional money has been going. Since 2024, spot Bitcoin ETFs have pulled in nearly $55 billion in inflows.

Gold and silver exchange-traded products, by comparison, have attracted around $29 billion over the same stretch. That puts Bitcoin funds at roughly double the precious metals haul.

Both Bitcoin and gold have recently shown a correlation of 60-70% with the S&P 500. In other words, when stocks fall, these two have tended to fall alongside them.

Timmer has not abandoned gold entirely. He continues to endorse both assets as tools for diversifying against monetary and fiscal instability.

His current lean toward Bitcoin is about near-term prospects. It is a tactical tilt, not a declaration that gold has lost its place in a portfolio.

For investors, the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio is a useful lens because it strips out the noise of the dollar. It shows how two competing hedges stack up against each other directly.

The recovery from about 12 ounces to about 21 ounces suggests the pendulum has swung back toward Bitcoin, at least for now. Timmer's own record of documented rotations, however, is a reminder that this pendulum has swung several times recently.

The most immediate takeaway is that a prominent Fidelity strategist sees Bitcoin holding its ground better than gold under pressure.

The ETF flow data supports the idea that institutions are already leaning this way. A gap of nearly $55 billion versus around $29 billion is hard to dismiss as a rounding error.

Yet the high correlation with stocks is a real risk. If both assets keep tracking the S&P 500 at 60-70%, their value as diversifiers shrinks during broad market drawdowns.

Timmer's position sits somewhere in the middle. He holds both as hedges against monetary and fiscal turbulence while tilting toward the one showing better relative strength.

data.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $411.9M on Friday as BlackRock Drives the Selling
data.description:
TL;DR: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net $411.9 million outflow on November 6, according to Farside Investors. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for $403 million in redemptions, while Fidelity’s FBTC attracted $42.8 million. The split matters more than a simplistic claim that every institutional investor was selling.

US Bitcoin exchange-traded funds ended the week with another difficult session. Farside Investors’ November 6 fund table shows $411.9 million leaving the group on a net basis, taking November’s first five trading sessions to approximately $1.28 billion in withdrawals. That is a meaningful reversal from the calmer periods in which ETF creations helped absorb supply.

But Friday’s figures tell a more interesting story than the headline total. The redemptions were highly concentrated, and one big issuer moved in the opposite direction.

BlackRock’s fund accounts for most of the outflow

IBIT recorded a $403 million net outflow on November 6. Bitwise’s BITB lost $20.5 million, ARK 21Shares’ ARKB lost $20.1 million and Grayscale’s GBTC lost $11.1 million. Against that, Fidelity’s FBTC brought in $42.8 million. Several other funds recorded zero flows in the published table. The sum produces a large negative number, but not a uniform retreat across products.

That distinction matters because an ETF creation or redemption is activity inside a particular listed vehicle. It tells us about changes in fund shares and exposure, not the identities of the investors involved or whether they immediately sold Bitcoin on an exchange. An asset manager could rebalance between issuers; a trading desk could adjust inventory; a portfolio could change its overall risk allocation. The public flow table does not resolve those motivations.

Earlier in the week, November 4 actually brought a $74.6 million net inflow, helped by a substantial positive day for Fidelity. Our coverage of November 2’s $398.6 million outflow documented a similarly concentrated session. The developing question is whether this is a persistent reduction in aggregate exposure or particularly volatile movement through a few large products.

Why repeated redemptions matter to Bitcoin

ETFs offer one of the clearest daily public windows into demand for regulated Bitcoin exposure. Repeated net withdrawals can weaken market confidence, particularly when liquidity is already thin or leveraged traders are reducing positions. Yet the ETF market is only one part of Bitcoin’s trading ecosystem. Spot exchanges, derivatives markets, corporate treasuries and long-term holders all affect the price.

It would also be a mistake to turn the week’s flow figures into a mechanical price prediction. Timing differs between trading, share creation, custody arrangements and hedge adjustments. Fund flows can accompany an existing move as readily as they can help drive one. The visible data establish a withdrawal from ETFs; they do not establish an inevitable next price level.

The fund-level split deserves continued attention. Fidelity’s positive session shows there were still buyers of this particular wrapper even as IBIT saw substantial redemptions. If outflows broaden to more issuers and persist for several sessions, the argument for a wider risk reduction becomes stronger. If the next week reverses, Friday could look more like a volatile reallocation.

The signals worth watching next

The next useful comparisons are net creations across the largest funds, aggregate trading volume and whether redemptions occur alongside lower spot liquidity. Readers should also distinguish a final daily figure from preliminary reporting as ETF data providers update their tables.

The deeper context is why these funds became so significant. As NewsBTC previously examined when Bitcoin hashrate rebounded, the network’s underlying activity and the investment products tracking its price operate on different timescales. For now, the verified conclusion is clear: November 6 was another outflow day, and BlackRock accounted for most of the selling pressure recorded within the ETF category.
